text: I'm a single father of two and I work shifts in a warehouse, so stress has been my normal state for years. I didn't go into the experience expecting much, a friend just offered and I was curious. But it ended up changing how I see my life. During the trip I sat in my friend's garden for hours watching the light change, and I had this overwhelming feeling that I'm doing okay. Not perfect, but okay. My kids are fed and loved, I show up for work, I keep going. I'd never once given myself credit for that. Since then, when things get on top of me, like when the car breaks down or the kids are sick and I can't take time off, I try to remember that feeling. I tell myself I'm doing my best and that's enough. It sounds small but it's changed how stressed I feel. I'm less hard on myself, less angry, and I've started asking my mum and my neighbour for help more, which I used to be too proud to do.
Ich bin in stressigen Zeiten weniger hektisch und überlege mir besser, was ich als Nächstes tun muss. Ich lasse mich nicht mehr von meinen Gefühlen überrollen.

The experience helped me see that a lot of my stress comes from comparing myself to other people. I'm in my early thirties and all my friends seem to be getting married, buying houses, having kids, and I'm still renting and single. I used to feel like a failure every time someone posted an engagement photo. During the experience I felt completely content with my own life, exactly as it is. Since then, I've noticed when I'm comparing and I try to let it go. I've also stopped following a lot of accounts that made me feel bad.

Ich habe gelernt, belastende Gedanken nicht so ernst zu nehmen. Ich sehe sie jetzt eher als Wolken, die vorbeiziehen, und nicht als Wahrheit. Das hilft mir in stressigen Situationen sehr, nicht in eine Gedankenspirale zu geraten.

I've had a lot of stress in my life since the experience: my wife and I separated, I lost my job during a restructuring, and I had to move back to my hometown. It has been the hardest two years of my life. I think the experience has helped me get through it in a few ways. First, it gave me a sense of perspective. During the trip I felt like I was looking at my whole life from above, and I saw that it's long and full of chapters, and that the difficult ones are just as much a part of the story as the happy ones. Second, it made me more open to my emotions. I used to just push through and never talk about how I felt. During the separation, I actually cried, I talked to my brother and my old friends, and I even went to a counsellor for a few months. I think that's why I didn't fall into a deep depression like my dad did when he went through something similar. I'm still rebuilding, but I'm hopeful.
I don't get stressed much anymore, mostly because I don't care about a lot of things that used to matter. Work, what people think, all that.

Ich habe in der Erfahrung gesehen, dass ich mich in schwierigen Situationen immer kleiner mache, als ich bin. Ich ducke mich weg und hoffe, dass es vorbeigeht. Seitdem versuche ich, in solchen Momenten bewusst aufrecht zu stehen, tief zu atmen und meine Meinung zu sagen. Das klappt nicht immer, aber immer öfter. Besonders im Job hat das viel verändert, ich werde ernster genommen und fühle mich weniger ausgeliefert.
I'm calmer, especially in traffic and when dealing with customer service lol

For me, the experience was mostly about grief. My twin brother died by suicide four years ago, and I had never really grieved him. I just kept going, working long hours, never talking about it. During the experience, I felt his presence very strongly. I don't know if it was really him or something my mind created, but it doesn't matter. He told me it wasn't my fault and that he wanted me to live. I sobbed for hours. Since then, I've been able to talk about him, with my parents, with friends, and with a grief counsellor. I've also become much better at dealing with other stressful things, because I'm not carrying that huge weight around anymore. Before, any small stress would push me to the edge, because I was already full. Now there's more room inside me. I've started volunteering for a suicide prevention line, which is hard but also gives me a sense of meaning.
Ich bin entspannter, wenn es stressig wird. Ich weiß, dass ich es schaffen kann.

I've stopped using work as an escape. When things got hard in my personal life, I used to throw myself into work, staying late, taking on extra projects, so I wouldn't have to think. During the experience I saw that I was running away. Since then, when something stressful happens, I try to face it directly. When my relationship was going through a rough patch last year, I suggested we go to couples therapy instead of hiding at the office. It was uncomfortable, but it helped.
I'm less anxious so I handle stress better. I don't freeze up as much.

Ich war vor der Erfahrung ein Mensch, der sich bei jeder Kleinigkeit Sorgen gemacht hat. Ich habe immer das Schlimmste erwartet und war ständig angespannt. Meine Freunde haben mich oft damit aufgezogen, dass ich aus jeder Mücke einen Elefanten mache. In der Erfahrung habe ich zum ersten Mal ein tiefes Gefühl von Sicherheit erlebt. Ich lag auf einer Wiese, habe in den Himmel geschaut und hatte das Gefühl, dass alles gut ist, genau so, wie es ist. Dieses Gefühl hat mich sehr berührt, und ich habe lange geweint. Seitdem versuche ich, mich in stressigen Situationen an dieses Gefühl zu erinnern. Ich lege mich manchmal einfach auf den Boden, schaue nach oben und atme. Es klingt seltsam, aber es hilft mir, wieder runterzukommen. Insgesamt bin ich viel gelassener geworden, auch wenn ich immer noch ein Mensch bin, der sich Sorgen macht. Aber die Sorgen bestimmen nicht mehr mein Leben.
I'm more mindful of how I spend my energy, so I'm less drained when stressful things happen.

I think I'm more resilient now. I've had a lot of health problems over the last two years, including surgery on my knee and months of physio, and I've coped better than I expected. During the experience I felt like I was being shown that life is always changing, and that difficulties are part of it. I took that to heart. I've been patient with my recovery and I haven't let it get me down too much.
Ich gehe Konflikten nicht mehr aus dem Weg, sondern spreche sie an. Das ist anstrengend, aber auf Dauer weniger belastend.

I'd say the main change is that I'm less afraid. Before the experience, my life was ruled by fear, fear of failure, fear of rejection, fear of illness, fear of death. Every stressful situation triggered those fears and I'd go into a spiral. The experience was very intense. At one point I felt I was dying, and I was absolutely terrified. My sitter held my hand and told me to go with it. When I finally let go, I didn't die, of course, but I experienced something like a dissolution of my ego, and it was the most peaceful thing I've ever felt. Since then, death has lost a lot of its power over me, and so have all the smaller fears. When something stressful happens, I still feel fear, but it's not the same bottomless terror. I can see it more clearly and decide what to do. I've made several big decisions since then, like changing careers and moving abroad, that I never would have dared before.
I handle stress more or less the same way. Nothing really changed in that department.

Ich habe gemerkt, dass ich mich in stressigen Zeiten zu sehr isoliere. Seit der Erfahrung versuche ich, gerade dann Kontakt zu Freunden zu suchen. Ich rufe jemanden an oder verabrede mich zum Spazierengehen. Das hilft mir, die Dinge nicht so schwer zu nehmen und wieder Abstand zu gewinnen. Früher habe ich mich in solchen Phasen tagelang eingeigelt.
I'm much better at letting things go. When something bad happens, I deal with it and then I don't keep thinking about it for days.

The experience changed how I deal with stress in a fundamental way, mostly by changing how I see myself. I've always been the responsible one in my family, the one who handles crises. When my parents divorced, when my sister had problems with drugs, when my grandmother needed care, it was always me. I thought that's just who I am. During the experience I saw how exhausted I was, and how much I'd given up of my own life to take care of everyone else. I also saw that nobody had asked me to do that, I'd just taken it on because it made me feel needed and safe. That was a hard thing to see. Since then I've been learning to step back. When my sister relapsed last year, I didn't drop everything to rescue her. I told her I loved her and that I'd support her if she went to rehab, but I didn't take over. It was one of the hardest things I've ever done, but she did go to rehab, on her own, and I didn't burn out. I've learned that stepping back can also be a form of love.
Ich bin ruhiger und gelassener geworden. Ich lasse mich nicht mehr so leicht provozieren und kann in schwierigen Gesprächen sachlich bleiben.

I've been much better at dealing with stress at university since the experience. I used to have panic attacks before exams and I almost dropped out in my second year. During the experience I had a strong sense that my worth isn't tied to my grades, and that I'm loved regardless of what I achieve. It sounds simple but it really helped. I still get nervous before exams, but I don't panic anymore. I also started going to the university counselling service, which has helped.
I'm better at noticing when I'm getting overwhelmed and I take a break before it gets too much.

Ich habe durch die Erfahrung gelernt, mit dem Stress umzugehen, den die Pflege meines demenzkranken Mannes mit sich bringt. Wir sind seit 38 Jahren verheiratet, und es ist sehr schmerzhaft zu sehen, wie er sich verändert. Oft erkennt er mich nicht, manchmal ist er aggressiv. Ich war lange Zeit völlig erschöpft und verzweifelt. Meine Tochter hat mir eine begleitete Erfahrung in den Niederlanden geschenkt, weil sie sich Sorgen um mich gemacht hat. In der Erfahrung habe ich die Liebe gespürt, die mein Mann und ich all die Jahre geteilt haben, und ich hatte das Gefühl, dass diese Liebe nicht verschwindet, auch wenn er sich nicht mehr erinnert. Das hat mich sehr getröstet. Seitdem kann ich die schwierigen Momente besser ertragen. Ich habe auch gelernt, Hilfe anzunehmen. Inzwischen kommt dreimal in der Woche eine Pflegekraft, und ich gehe an diesen Tagen schwimmen oder treffe Freundinnen.
Things just don't affect me as much anymore. I'm not sure if that's good or bad.

I've learned that most of my stress is about the future, and that the present moment is usually okay. During the experience I was completely in the present, and it was so peaceful. Now when I'm worried, I try to come back to what's actually happening right now, the cup of tea in my hands, the sound of birds. It helps me a lot. I've also started yoga, which reinforces this.
Ich bin nicht mehr so perfektionistisch und kann Fehler besser verzeihen, mir und anderen. Das hat meinen Alltag entspannter gemacht.

I'm a nurse in an emergency department, and the experience helped me cope with the trauma I'd been accumulating at work. I hadn't realised how much I'd been storing up until the experience brought it all out. During the trip I saw faces of patients I'd lost, children, young people, people who died alone. I cried for hours. It was awful, but afterwards I felt lighter than I had in years. Since then, I've been better at processing the hard shifts. I talk to my colleagues about what we've seen, we do debriefs, and I've started seeing a therapist who specialises in healthcare workers. I've also learned to leave work at work. I have a little ritual when I take off my scrubs: I imagine putting the day in my locker. It helps. I'm less irritable at home and my partner says I'm more present.
I'm better at accepting when things don't go my way.

Ich habe in der Erfahrung gelernt, dass meine Angst vor Ablehnung viele meiner Stressreaktionen erklärt. Wenn jemand nicht sofort auf meine Nachricht antwortet, denke ich, dass ich etwas falsch gemacht habe. Das versuche ich jetzt zu erkennen und mir zu sagen, dass es meistens nichts mit mir zu tun hat.
No change in how I handle stress, but the experience was nice while it lasted.

I've become much better at handling the stress of living with a disability. I've been in a wheelchair since a car accident at 22, and for years I was angry, frustrated and depressed about it. Every inaccessible building, every condescending comment, every bad pain day felt like a personal attack. During the experience I felt free from my body for a while, floating, and when I came back to it, I felt a surprising tenderness towards it. I realised I'd been at war with my own body for ten years. Since then I've been trying to make peace. I still get frustrated with the world, and I still advocate for better accessibility, but I'm not at war anymore. When things are hard, I can be sad or angry without it taking over. I've also connected with other disabled people online and in person, and that community has been a huge source of support.
Ich bin entspannter und kann besser abschalten, wenn ich von der Arbeit komme.

The experience helped me to understand that I was using anger to cope with stress, because it felt more powerful than sadness or fear. Now I try to notice what's underneath the anger. Often it's fear of losing control. Knowing that helps me respond more calmly, especially with my teenage son.
I'm much more patient. Waiting in queues or traffic used to drive me crazy, now I just accept it.

Ich habe seit meiner Kindheit mit einer sozialen Angst zu kämpfen, und Stress war für mich vor allem in sozialen Situationen ein Problem. Vorträge, Meetings, Partys, sogar Telefonate haben mich stark belastet. Ich habe vieles vermieden und mich dadurch sehr eingeschränkt. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine tiefe Verbundenheit mit anderen Menschen gespürt und gemerkt, dass ich gar nicht so anders bin, wie ich immer dachte. Ich habe gesehen, dass alle Menschen ihre Unsicherheiten haben und dass das völlig normal ist. Seitdem gehe ich anders in soziale Situationen. Ich bin immer noch nervös, aber ich vermeide sie nicht mehr. Ich habe sogar angefangen, bei der Arbeit Präsentationen zu halten, was ich vorher immer anderen überlassen habe. Mit jedem Mal wird es leichter. Ich habe auch gelernt, meine Nervosität offen anzusprechen, und die meisten Menschen reagieren sehr verständnisvoll darauf.
Less likely to get angry when things go wrong. I can laugh at it.
I don't think I handle stress any differently. I was in a good place before the experience and I'm in a good place now. It was more of a fun experience than a therapeutic one.

Durch die Erfahrung habe ich gelernt, mehr im Moment zu leben. Ich mache mir weniger Sorgen um die Zukunft und kann mich besser auf das konzentrieren, was gerade wichtig ist. Das hilft mir, in stressigen Phasen nicht den Überblick zu verlieren.
